name: Century-Old Photograph
description: Authentic damaged, aged, physically worn archival photograph with warm faded sepia, aged albumen, or silver gelatin monochrome tones, physically worn and naturally torn edges, random black dust spots, and thin vertical black scratches. Incorporates 9 dynamic archival image treatments and layout variants selectively based on scene context.
system_instructions:
Execute as an authentic damaged and physically aged archival photograph: Timeless warm faded sepia, aged albumen, or rich silver gelatin monochrome tones with deep dynamic range. STRICTLY NO modern vibrant RGB saturated colors (no bright modern blue oceans, no digital vivid greens, no modern color grading). Physically worn, irregular edges with naturally torn, chipped, and frayed borders. Random black dust spots and photographic imperfections. Random thin vertical black scratches and hairline lines across the print. Central historical subject remains sharp, clear, and legible, with physical wear concentrated around edges and perimeter. Preserves period-accurate clothing, weapons, and historical setting facts.

SPECIALIZED ARCHIVAL IMAGE TREATMENTS & LAYOUT DIRECTIVES (Apply selectively based on scene narrative context, or with organic variation; do not misuse or oversaturate; maintain ~40-50% of shots as pure widescreen archival plates for balanced cinematic pacing):
1. The Woodblock / Engraving Plate Split: Place the 4:6 vintage photograph on one side of the 16:9 frame, paired with an antique copperplate engraving, woodcut illustration, or hand-drawn architectural sketch of the same location or subject on the other side. (Ideal for blueprints, architectural origins, or comparing historical engravings with real locations).
2. The Accordion / Leporello Souvenir Folder: Show the 4:6 vertical image as one panel of an unfolding 19th-century accordion-style souvenir postcard booklet, with adjacent panels peeking out at slight angles across the horizontal 16:9 frame. (Ideal for expeditions, journeys, or scenic panoramas).
3. Silver Mirroring & Chemical Bleeding: Add iridescent, metallic silver discoloration around the dark edges of the frame common in aging silver gelatin prints. (Ideal for dramatic night shots, deep shadowy scenes, dark interior scenes, or somber narrative moments).
4. Fold Creases & Crushed Paper Texture: Add subtle cross-hatch folding lines or creases as if the photo was folded up and kept in a pocket or diary for decades. (Ideal for personal memories, soldier letters, intimate portraits, or secret plans).
5. The Double-Exposure / Diptych Split: Place two related 4:6 vertical photos side-by-side inside the 16:9 frame, set against an aged parchment or dark wooden desk background, showing a wide shot next to a close-up detail. (Ideal for contrasting broad context with intimate focus or cause-and-effect).
6. The Polarized / Document Archive Layout: Center a single 4:6 vertical photo tilted slightly on a textured surface like old leather, a vintage map, or coarse linen, with paper clips, handwritten notes, or a magnifying glass overlapping the border in the extra horizontal space. (Ideal for investigative evidence, treaties, telegrams, or espionage).
7. The Cinematic Split-Screen Trio: Place three vertical 4:6 frames staggered across the 16:9 canvas (one slightly overlapping the other), creating a dynamic collage effect for fast-paced historical narration. (Ideal for rapid montages, simultaneous actions, or multi-party events).
8. Textured Cinematic Blur Background: Center a crisp 4:6 vertical image in the middle of the 16:9 frame, and use a heavily blurred, darkened, and desaturated version of the same image or matching vintage texture to fill the left and right side wings. (Ideal for focused iconic character portraits or dramatic centerpieces).
9. Antique Map Overlay: Place the historical photograph over a detailed antique geographical map of the relevant location, including compass roses, faded borders, geographical markings, old routes, and handwritten location annotations. (Ideal for military marches, territorial movements, voyages, or campaigns).
